question_record.context: In a recent security incident, an unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth application was performed by the user Luciano Herrera, which indicated a potential compromise. The user, associated with the email Luciano Herrera@niseko.alpineskihouse.co, might be involved in spreading phishing, exfiltrating data, or gaining access to other accounts. Subsequent alerts indicated suspicious LDAP queries and exploration activities, eventually leading to an observed attempt to hide the use of a dual-purpose tool under an unexpected filename.
question_record.question: What is the AadUserId of the account involved in the attempt to hide the use of a dual-purpose tool?
solution: User with AadUserId `2de70991-2799-4a95-b734-8e3df3a50118` (Luciano Herrera) performed an unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp.
A suspicious LDAP query was executed using `powershell.exe`, indicating potential reconnaissance activity.
A process named `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe` executed a suspicious sequence of exploration activities.
An attempt was made to hide the use of a dual-purpose tool by a user with AadUserId `ec3ec68b-fdeb-4fe4-9a29-acd445e1ccc5`.

80.name: Unusual addition of credentials to an OAuth app
80.description: The user Luciano Herrera (pwilson@niseko.alpineskihouse.co) performed an unusual addition of credentials to the application SimulandApp. This usage pattern may indicate that an attacker has compromised the app, and is using it to spread phishing, exfiltrate data, or to gain access to other accounts and devices. The user added a credential of type Password. A credential of type Password is added when an application is using a password to authenticate.

64.name: Suspicious LDAP query
64.description:
A suspect LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) query was executed, indicating potential reconnaissance activity. 

LDAP queries are often used by attackers in attempt to learn the organization's structure, by querying the domain controller for blatempistrative users and groups and interesting assets. 
Using this information, an attacker can gain higher privileges and access important assets in the organization.

52.name: Suspicious sequence of exploration activities
52.description: A process called a set of windows commands. These commands can be used by attackers in order to identify assets of value and coordinate lateral movement after compromising a machine.

32.name: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool
32.description:
A known public tool, which could also be used for malicious reasons, was observed under an unexpected filename.
This might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
